sentences.t: News Report 1. A man was left with a $1,000 bill after his 6-year-old son ordered a virtual buffet of food from several restaurants last weekend.
This led to a string of unexpected deliveries and maybe a starring role in an advertisement campaign.
Keith Stonehouse said the food piled up quickly at his home Saturday night after he let his son use his cell phone to play a game before bed.
He said the youngster instead used his father's online food ordering account to order food from one restaurant after another.
The boy's mother, Kristen Stonehouse, said that the online food app has reached out to the family and offered them a $1,000 gift card.
The company also is considering using the family in an online promotional campaign.
Most of the food went into the family's refrigerators. They also invited some neighbors over to eat some of it.
The father is planning to change his password.

sentences.t: News report 2. Animal behavior experts looked at more than 100 research papers.
They examined how visitors affected the behavior of more than 250 species in zoos.
They found that elephants socialized more with each other during public feeding times.
After public feeding times, they were more likely to search for food and less likely to be inactive.
In the presence of many visitors, elephants were less likely to use repetitive behaviors which often indicate boredom.
Visitors had a similar effect on some other species too, including polar bears,
certain jungle cats, and black-tailed, plain dogs.
Some animal species have been born and raised in zoos, and so have likely become used to the presence of humans.
Zoo visitors are often aspects of zoo animals' environment that animals cannot control and, as such, can be stressful.
although some species appear to show good adaptability to the changing conditions of visitors.

sentences.t: Conversation 2.
Can you give me advice about being successful at a new job? I start mine next week.
Sure. It's important not to undermine the significance of the first few days of your job, since this is the best time to create a solid first impression.
That's a good point. I'll need to collaborate with my co-workers, and I'm very aware of just how important others are for my success at work.
It's also important to understand your role thoroughly to gain a comprehensive picture of your job.
The most important thing for you to do at first is to understand your role from multiple perspectives.
Why is that?
Well, what you do at work is not just limited to your job description.
You need to consider how your work relates to other people within the organization.
Oh right. So for example, certain reports that I create at the end of the month may be used by a team in another department.
That's right. And in that respect, it's also important to learn about the business to see the big picture.
You mean like knowing about the history of the company?
Kind of, but more like knowing the details of the products and services that the company
exists to deliver.
Learning about the business will give you a chance to understand how your role fits into
the bigger picture.
Okay, I'm feeling a bit uneasy about meeting my boss as well.
That's to be expected.
However, it's crucial that you get to know the people who have decision-making authority
to gain insight regarding how the business is run and decisions are made.
Great advice. Thanks.
